access_model: Self-serve developer account and personal token; free developer account available for API testing. Hosted MCP is available on all plans at no additional cost, but account AI Connector permissions/admin policy and user consent govern access.
api_type: GraphQL API v2 and official hosted remote MCP server (Streamable HTTP).
api_breadth: GraphQL API covers boards, workspaces, items, columns, users and account data; hosted MCP provides 60+ read/write tools through the authenticated user's permissions.
existing_mcp: Official — hosted MCP endpoint https://mcp.monday.com/mcp; Streamable HTTP only. Older /sse transport is deprecated and unsupported.
main_blocker: User-context permissions and organization controls; custom OAuth clients may require dynamic registration/admin approval. Personal tokens inherit user permissions and must be protected.
verification_note: First-party docs confirm hosted MCP endpoint, Streamable HTTP, OAuth/API-token paths, dynamic connectors, 60+ tools and all-plan availability. Personal tokens mirror user's UI permissions; deprecated SSE URLs should not be used.

description: Work management platform combining tasks, docs, goals, chat, dashboards and workflow automation.
auth_methods: OAuth 2.1 with PKCE for official MCP; OAuth 2.0 for public integrations; personal API tokens for direct REST API use.
access_model: MCP is available on all plans and supports OAuth only; direct REST API use requires a ClickUp account and API token or registered OAuth app. Workspace permissions and MCP rate limits apply.
api_type: Public REST API and official hosted remote MCP server.
api_breadth: REST API covers workspaces, spaces, folders, lists, tasks, comments, users, time tracking and goals; MCP exposes task, list, doc and workspace workflows.
existing_mcp: Official — hosted endpoint https://mcp.clickup.com/mcp; OAuth only, no personal API token authentication for MCP.
main_blocker: MCP supports OAuth only and has workspace rate limits; REST API token auth is separate. Workspace permissions and plan-specific feature limits still apply.
verification_note: First-party docs confirm all-plan MCP, endpoint, OAuth-only auth and rate limiting. Do not confuse direct REST API personal tokens with MCP authentication.

description: Collaborative document platform with tables, interactive apps, formulas, automations and connected packs.
auth_methods: OAuth 2 for supported clients; Personal Access Tokens restricted to MCP with read-only, write-only or read/write scope; REST API uses API tokens.
access_model: MCP is beta. Doc Makers on paid plans have full MCP tools; Doc Makers on free plans receive a limited free taste (30 requests/week, max 60/month). Admins can disable new app connections; access follows the user's Coda role and doc permissions.
api_type: Public REST API and official hosted MCP server at https://coda.io/apis/mcp.
api_breadth: REST API covers docs, pages, tables, rows, columns, formulas, controls and permissions; MCP supports reading and writing docs and tables, with tool availability and limits dependent on role/plan.
existing_mcp: Official — Coda MCP hosted endpoint https://coda.io/apis/mcp; OAuth 2 for ChatGPT/Claude/Cursor and PAT for Codex/other clients.
main_blocker: MCP is beta and paid Doc Makers receive the full experience; free Doc Makers have strict request caps. Document permissions and admin app controls apply.
verification_note: Coda first-party MCP guide confirms endpoint, supported clients/auth methods, beta status, admin disablement and free-tier request caps. Keep MCP tool coverage distinct from REST API breadth.

description: Enterprise work management platform for project plans, sheets, dashboards, forms, resource management and automated workflows.
auth_methods: Bearer API access tokens for personal integrations; OAuth 2.0 three-legged flow for integrations requiring user consent.
access_model: Self-serve API access token generation in Personal Settings; account/region-specific tokens (including Gov and EU regions). OAuth requires user authorization; API use is subject to account permissions and limits.
api_type: Public REST API. Official MCP server not verified in reviewed first-party docs.
api_breadth: REST API covers sheets, rows, columns, attachments, comments, users, workspaces, reports and dashboards; exact access depends on account permissions and product entitlements.
existing_mcp: Not verified — no official Smartsheet MCP server confirmed in reviewed first-party developer documentation.
main_blocker: Account permissions, region-specific token handling and API limits; OAuth consent is needed for third-party user-authorized integrations.
verification_note: First-party docs confirm Bearer API access tokens and recommend OAuth where user consent is needed. MCP status remains unverified; do not treat community servers as official.

description: Time-tracking and invoicing platform for tracking projects, expenses, budgets, clients and billable work.
auth_methods: Personal Access Token (Bearer) for scripts; OAuth 2.0 authorization-code flow for integrations used by other accounts.
access_model: Self-serve developer token creation; PAT has all-account scope by default. Multi-user integrations require OAuth app registration, redirect URL and user consent; account/product scopes limit access.
api_type: Public REST API v2. Official MCP server not verified in reviewed first-party docs.
api_breadth: REST API covers time entries, projects, tasks, clients, users, invoices, estimates, expenses, and reports; account ID is required for most requests.
existing_mcp: Not verified — no official Harvest MCP server confirmed in reviewed first-party API documentation.
main_blocker: Account ID and scope handling; PAT grants broad account access, while multi-user integrations need OAuth registration and token refresh handling.
verification_note: Current first-party Harvest API v2 docs confirm PAT and OAuth2, Bearer header, account ID, OAuth refresh flow and scope model. MCP remains unverified.

Restricted API keys
OAuth 2.0 for Connect platforms

Webhooks

Bearer access tokens for specific OAuth-related endpoints
Link public_token exchanged for access_token

Webhooks
MCP (Sandbox and Dashboard MCP)

main_blocker: Production access approval and institution/product eligibility; Trial plan is region-limited and capped.
verification_note: Plaid docs confirm client_id/secret, Link token exchange, free Sandbox, official Sandbox MCP and Dashboard MCP production approval. Trial eligibility is limited to US/Canada; do not generalize to global self-serve.

description: Cryptocurrency exchange offering spot and other trading products, market data, account services and developer APIs.
auth_methods: Public market-data endpoints need no credentials; private endpoints use API key plus request signature (HMAC, RSA or Ed25519 depending on key type). API keys have configurable permissions.
access_model: API docs are public, but private API keys require a Binance account, identity verification, 2FA and account activation steps; trading/withdrawal permissions require additional security controls and may be region/account restricted.
api_type: Official REST APIs, WebSocket streams and FIX API; official Binance Agentic MCP endpoint also documented.
api_breadth: Broad product-specific APIs for market data, account balances, orders, trades, deposits/withdrawals, streams and related exchange functions; endpoints and eligibility vary by product and jurisdiction.
existing_mcp: Official — Binance Agentic MCP endpoint https://agent.binance.com/mcp/agentic; supports market data and eligible Agentic sub-account operations subject to authorization and eligibility.
main_blocker: KYC/account eligibility, strict API-key permissions and jurisdiction restrictions; trading and fund-transfer actions are high-risk and require explicit user authorization and secure key handling.
verification_note: Official Binance docs confirm REST/WebSocket/FIX interfaces and API key/signature requirements. Binance's own MCP article documents the Agentic MCP endpoint and states operations depend on account eligibility/authorization. Distinguish this narrow Agentic MCP from full exchange API coverage.

api_breadth: FX audit and rate lookup endpoints, document audit workflow and webhook event delivery; docs show transaction-batch audit input, usage metadata and partner-rate comparison.
existing_mcp: Advertised marketplace/MCP compatibility, but no dedicated official MCP endpoint or server implementation was verified in the reviewed developer documentation.
main_blocker: Young/narrow API surface and inconsistent public documentation paths/base URLs across pages; validate the current canonical endpoint, schema, pricing and production SLA before committing.
verification_note: First-party docs confirm Bearer keys, webhook signing and FX audit API. The docs show more than one API path/base URL, and the API terms page is marked draft; treat endpoint and commercial details as provisional. MCP is advertised but not independently verified as a callable server.

Bearer access tokens
Refresh tokens

GraphQL (Intuit ecosystem / docs indicate QBO and Intuit Financial Ecosystem)

auth_methods: OAuth 2.0 authorization code
OAuth 2.0 PKCE
Client credentials for non-tenanted app-data endpoints
access_model: Self-serve developer registration and demo company; connecting customer organisations requires OAuth consent. Commercial tiers and connection limits apply from March 2026.
api_type: REST
Webhooks
MCP

verification_note: Current Xero docs confirm OAuth code/PKCE, official hosted MCP, tier limits and fees, Starter demo-only MCP access, and restrictions on API data use for AI/ML training. Pricing and terms must be rechecked at submission date.

description: Financial operations platform for businesses, including corporate cards, spend management, reimbursements, bill pay, travel and business accounts.
auth_methods: User API tokens (Bearer) for a company's own account; OAuth 2.0/OpenID Connect authorization-code flow for partner apps; official MCP supports OAuth and scoped API tokens.
access_model: Requires a Brex business account with Developer API access enabled; account/card admin must accept the Developer API agreement and create tokens. Partner integrations require Brex developer-partner onboarding and customer authorization. MCP is early-access/beta and admin-enabled.
api_type: Public REST APIs and official hosted remote MCP server.
api_breadth: REST APIs cover team, cards, transactions, expenses, reimbursements, accounting and onboarding workflows; MCP exposes selected AI-facing tools such as expense queries, user lookup and card-status checks.

main_blocker: Business-account/admin gate, Developer API agreement and early-access enablement for MCP; partner OAuth requires appropriate partner status and customer roles/scopes.
verification_note: Brex first-party docs distinguish user tokens from partner OAuth and describe admin setup, token scopes and expiration. Official support/changelog docs confirm MCP endpoint, OAuth/API-token support and early-access enablement; do not describe MCP as universally self-serve.

description: Corporate spend management platform for cards, expenses, bill pay, procurement and finance operations.
auth_methods: Developer API uses OAuth 2.0 client credentials for a company’s own Ramp account; partner integrations use OAuth authorization. Ramp MCP uses interactive OAuth sign-in with Full access or Read-only selection.
access_model: Public developer documentation; existing Ramp customers need an admin to create developer apps and grant scopes. Sandbox access can be requested. Production partner integrations require developer-console approval.
api_type: Official REST Developer API; official hosted Ramp MCP at https://mcp.ramp.com/mcp; separate Ramp Data MCP and CLI.
api_breadth: Broad finance operations including transactions, cards, users, reimbursements, bills, approvals and spend workflows; exact endpoint access depends on enabled scopes and Ramp role. MCP tools are permission-filtered.
existing_mcp: Official — Ramp-hosted MCP documented by Ramp, with read-only/full-access modes.
main_blocker: Admin access needed to create developer apps; production integrations for other Ramp businesses require partner review. MCP connection requires user role permission and expires after 30 days.
verification_note: Official Ramp docs specify admin-created developer apps, OAuth client credentials/scopes, sandbox and production flows, and the hosted MCP endpoint. No live tenant authentication or API call was performed.

api_type: Official RESTful API at https://api.pitchbook.com; no public GraphQL interface or official MCP server verified in the reviewed sources.

main_blocker: Commercial contract and vendor-led provisioning make access non-self-serve; API endpoint breadth and credentials are not fully inspectable before onboarding.
verification_note: PitchBook's own help page explicitly says the API is a separate offering requiring a standalone contract, describes it as RESTful with base URL https://api.pitchbook.com, and says access is arranged through Direct Data or the client platform. The page mentions API keys or authentication tokens. No MCP claim is made because none was established by this source.

description: Google's source-grounded notebook and research assistant for organizing documents, web sources and other reference material; the product/API naming is transitioning to Gemini Notebook.
auth_methods: Google OAuth 2.0 access token with the https://www.googleapis.com/auth/notebook scope; Application Default Credentials setup also requires a Google Cloud project and x-goog-user-project header.
access_model: Partially self-serve but cloud-project gated. The official Gemini Notebook API MCP requires enabling notebook.googleapis.com, a Google Cloud project, a personal Google Account that has signed in to the notebook product, and OAuth scope setup. Google Workspace accounts are stated as not yet supported in the MCP quickstart.
api_type: Official remote Streamable HTTP MCP server at https://notebook.googleapis.com/mcp; Google documents a corresponding Gemini Notebook API. No public consumer-app REST/GraphQL surface should be assumed beyond the documented API.
api_breadth: Official MCP exposes seven tools for notebook creation, retrieval/listing/updating and source ingestion/retrieval/listing. Sources include web URLs, YouTube, plain text and Markdown; file upload is not exposed as an MCP tool and uses a separate REST upload endpoint.
existing_mcp: Official — Google Gemini Notebook API MCP at https://notebook.googleapis.com/mcp. This is Google's official API/MCP surface; confirm current product naming because the assignment's NotebookLM label may refer to the earlier product name.
main_blocker: Requires Google Cloud project/API enablement and scoped OAuth/ADC setup; one-hour access-token expiry adds operational refresh work. Workspace-account support is limited in the current quickstart.
verification_note: Current official API is named Gemini Notebook API. Official MCP endpoint is https://notebook.googleapis.com/mcp; OAuth scope is notebook. Public preview currently requires personal Google account and a prior sign-in to Gemini Notebook; Workspace accounts are unsupported.
audit_note: Current official API is named Gemini Notebook API. Official MCP endpoint is https://notebook.googleapis.com/mcp; OAuth scope is notebook. Public preview currently requires personal Google account and a prior sign-in to Gemini Notebook; Workspace accounts are unsupported.

description: AI meeting assistant that records, transcribes and summarizes conversations, with searchable transcripts and meeting intelligence.
auth_methods: OAuth is required for the hosted MCP connection. The Public API uses Bearer-token authentication with an API key created in Integrations → Developer.
access_model: Split access. Otter MCP can be connected by URL and requires account authorization, but Otter says availability across AI applications is still being rolled out and support may be required. The Public API is restricted to Enterprise workspaces and may require admin permissions.
api_type: Official Public API documented by Otter; hosted MCP server at https://mcp.otter.ai/mcp. No GraphQL interface verified.
api_breadth: Public API supports retrieval of channels, conversations, transcripts, audio, action items, insights, outlines and workspace details. MCP tools documented by Otter include user info, meeting search and transcript fetch.
existing_mcp: Official — Otter MCP server at https://mcp.otter.ai/mcp. Vendor help documentation provides the endpoint and describes Search, Fetch and user-info tools.
main_blocker: The broad Public API is Enterprise-only; MCP availability depends on supported client/platform and OAuth/account permissions, and Otter states it is still expanding availability. Access to a meeting is limited by sharing/workspace permissions.
verification_note: Both the MCP server and Public API are described in Otter's own Help Center. Do not label the Public API generally self-serve: the official article says Enterprise plan required. MCP OAuth is required, and Otter notes availability for AI applications is still being released.

description: AI meeting assistant that records, transcribes and summarizes video meetings and extracts action items and follow-up context.

api_breadth: MCP provides meeting-context retrieval for meetings the user can view and supports drafting/synthesis workflows. The reviewed help article does not enumerate the complete MCP tool inventory; a separate API surface is documented by Fathom.
existing_mcp: Official — Fathom hosted MCP at https://api.fathom.ai/mcp; Fathom's own help center and product page document the integration.
main_blocker: Access is constrained by per-user/team meeting permissions; complete MCP tool inventory and REST credential details need a live authenticated check before promising specific actions.
verification_note: Fathom's own help center, edited November 19, 2026, documents MCP setup and states assistants can access only meetings the user has permission to view. Fathom's product page states the hosted MCP is available on every plan, including Free, and provides the endpoint. The help article does not enumerate tools, so breadth is intentionally described conservatively.

description: Transcript and caption extraction for YouTube videos; exact product/vendor identity is ambiguous in the supplied app name.
auth_methods: For YouTube's official captions API, OAuth 2.0 is required for caption listing/download operations; third-party transcript services may use separate API keys.

existing_mcp: Not verified for a specifically named YouTube Transcript product. Third-party MCP wrappers may exist but are not treated as official YouTube MCP.
main_blocker: Official caption download is restricted to users with edit permission on the video; app identity is ambiguous and no third-party vendor/API was specified.
verification_note: Official YouTube Data API captions.download requires OAuth authorization and permission to edit the video; it does not provide a general method to download captions from arbitrary public videos. The dataset label YouTube Transcript is therefore mapped only to the official captions API capability; third-party transcript providers are outside this verification.
